arxiv-2302-06108.title: Animating Human Athletics
arxiv-2302-06108.creator: Jessica K. Hodgins Wayne L. Wooten David C. Brogan James F. O’Brien
arxiv-2302-06108.description: Abstract 0 0 footnotetext: College of Computing, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA 30332-0280. [jkh | wlw | dbrogan | obrienj]@cc.gatech.edu ABSTRACT This paper describes algorithms for the animation of men and women performing three dynamic athletic behaviors: running, bicycling, and vaulting. We animate these behaviors using control algorithms that cause a physically realistic model to perform the desired maneuver.

arxiv-2407-18237.title: Heterogeneous model for superdiffusive movement of dense-core vesicles in C. elegans
arxiv-2407-18237.creator: Anna Gavrilova, Nickolay Korabel, Victoria J. Allan, Sergei Fedotov
arxiv-2407-18237.description: Abstract Transport of dense core vesicles (DCVs) in neurons is crucial for distributing molecules like neuropeptides and growth factors. We studied the experimental trajectories of dynein-driven directed movement of DCVs in the ALA neuron C. elegans over a duration of up to 6 seconds. We analysed the DCV movement in three strains of C.

arxiv-2409-06092.title: A Census of the β \beta Pic Moving Group and Other Nearby Associations with Gaia
arxiv-2409-06092.creator: K. L. Luhman
arxiv-2409-06092.description: Abstract I have used the third data release of the Gaia mission to improve the reliability and completeness of membership samples in the β \beta Pic moving group (BPMG) and other nearby associations with ages of 20–50 Myr (Sco Body, Carina, Columba, χ 1 \chi^{1} For, Tuc-Hor, IC 2602, IC 2391, NGC 2547).

arxiv-2506-15995.title: Pion Valence Structure at Intermediate x in the Residual Field Model
arxiv-2506-15995.creator: Joseph Maerovitz, Alan Sosa, Misak Sargsian, Christopher Leon
arxiv-2506-15995.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joseph Maerovitz, Alan Sosa, Misak Sargsian, Christopher Leon. We calculate the valence parton distribution function of the pion, for the range of 0.1 ≤ x ≤ 0.6 0.1\leq x\leq 0.6 , based on the soft dynamics of the partons within the valence-residual field model. Within this model we assume that the soft partonic structure of the pion is defined by the valence current q ​ q ¯ q\bar{q} cluster embedded in the residual field of the pion.

arxiv-2506-23011.title: Effects of Large Optical Depth on CD H i 21-cm Non-Gaussian Signal 2026 Effects of Large Optical Depth on CD H i 21-cm Non-Gaussian Signal – References
arxiv-2506-23011.creator: Iffat Nasreen, Kanan K. Datta, Abinash K. Shaw, Leon Noble, Raghunath Ghara, Sk. Saiyad Ali, Arnab Mishra, Mohd Kamran, Suman Majumdar
arxiv-2506-23011.description: Abstract During the Cosmic Dawn (CD), the HI 21-cm optical depth ( τ \tau ) in the intergalactic medium can become significantly large. Consequently, the second and higher-order terms of τ \tau appearing in the Taylor expansion of the HI 21-cm differential brightness temperature ( δ ​ T b \delta T_{\rm b} ) become important.

arxiv-2512-11390.title: A Molecular Gas Dynamics Study of Hypersonic Boundary Layer Second Mack Mode Instabilities
arxiv-2512-11390.creator: Mert Senkardesler, Irmak T. Karpuzcu, Deborah A. Levin, Vassilis Theofilis
arxiv-2512-11390.description: Abstract A flat-plate laminar boundary layer is simulated at Mach 6 and unit Reynolds number R ​ e 1 ∼ 1.1 × 10 7 Re_{1}\sim 1.1\times 10^{7} m -1 using the Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method to capture and analyze spontaneous second-mode instability growth.

arxiv-2512-22617.title: Evidence for a Stratified Accretion Disk Wind in AGN Volume: 54
arxiv-2512-22617.creator: P. Marziani \orcid 0000-0002-6058-4912, E. Bon, S. Panda, N. Bon, A. Del Olmo, A. Deconto-Machado, K. Garnica, D. Dultzin
arxiv-2512-22617.description: Abstract We present observational evidence supporting the presence of a stratified accretion disk wind in active galactic nuclei (AGN), based on multi-wavelength spectroscopic analysis of broad and narrow emission lines. The diversity in emission line profiles, ionization potentials, and kinematic signatures suggests a structured outflow emerging from the accretion disk, with different zones contributing to specific spectral features.

pmc-10642033.title: “I know what I'm supposed to do, but I don't do it”: patient-perceived risk factors that lead to their lower extremity amputations
pmc-10642033.creator: Marcelle Ben chmo, Lisa Matricciani, Saravana Kumar, Kristin Graham
pmc-10642033.description: BackgroundThe purpose of this study is to extend on our previous research by exploring patient-perceived factors that lead to their Lower Extremity Amputations (LEA). LEA are a serious complication of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), LEA are thought to be preventable with early detection and management of risk factors.

pmc-10647359.title: Updates on Pathophysiology of Discogenic Back Pain
pmc-10647359.creator: Rohan Jha, Joshua D. Bernstock, Joshua I. Chalif, Samantha E. Hoffman, Saksham Gupta, Hong Guo, Yi Lu
pmc-10647359.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Discogenic back pain, a subset of chronic back pain, is caused by intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration, and imparts a notable socioeconomic health burden on the population. However, degeneration by itself does not necessarily imply discogenic pain. In this review, we highlight the existing literature on the pathophysiology of discogenic back pain, focusing on the biomechanical and biochemical steps that lead to pain in the setting of IVD degeneration.

pmc-10737148.title: UTILIZING PALLIATIVE LEADERS IN FACILITIES TO TRANSFORM CARE: THE UPLIFT CLINICAL TRIAL IMPLEMENTATION
pmc-10737148.creator: Kathleen Unroe, John Cagle, Mary Ersek
pmc-10737148.description: UPLIFT is an NIH funded clinical trial with a goal of improving quality of care for people with moderate to advanced dementia in nursing homes. The UPLIFT intervention consists of specialized training in palliative care and dementia care for two nursing facility staff who are identified as Palliative Care Leads.

pmc-11472468.title: 5-Hydroxyindoleacetic acid as a biomarker for revealing perforation in acute appendicitis
pmc-11472468.creator: Arash Mohammadi Tofigh, Majid Samsami, Alireza Haghbin Toutounchi, Shervin Tavakoli, Zeinab Taabzadeh, Hojatolah Khoshnoudi, Ehsan Adinevand
pmc-11472468.description: BackgroundThe present study investigated the level of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) in perforated and nonperforated appendicitis patients. This issue is important for timely diagnosis of acute appendicitis complications and making decision about the surgical plan and type of incision.MethodsThis prospective study was conducted on patients with acute appendicitis.

pmc-12699444.title: Closed Flexor Tendon Avulsions Associated With a Distal Radius Fracture: A Case Report
pmc-12699444.creator: Ross McAllister, Natan Silver, Daniel Brown
pmc-12699444.description: Flexor tendon injuries have been reported in association with distal radius fractures. These are usually chronic in nature, and acute flexor tendon injuries are rare. When these do occur, they tend to be at the level of the fracture and are thought to be caused by direct laceration from the sharp bone edges of the fracture site.

pmc-13086656.title: Benefits of a brief, remote psychoeducation intervention in treating eating disorders: a preliminary study in a predominantly AN/BN sample
pmc-13086656.creator: Laurent Cruchet, Lucia Romo, Philibert Duriez, Maria Alejandra Laszcz, Daphnée Poupon, Philip Gorwood
pmc-13086656.description: PurposeEngagement in care is particularly problematic among patients suffering from eating disorders (ED). We aimed to assess whether a brief, remote, psychoeducation (PE) intervention could facilitate engagement and/or potentiate treatment. We also aimed to study whether the acquisition of knowledge, a key aspect of PE, could relate to its efficacy.

pmc-13673922.title: Prevalence and predictors of percent body fat-defined obesity among federal contingency force commandos in India: implications for military obesity standards
pmc-13673922.creator: Devika Bhat, Rakshit Shah, Mihir Rupani, Nitishkumar Tank, Ankit Sheth, Ankit Viramgami, Sanjay Kotadiya
pmc-13673922.description: BackgroundObesity is increasingly affecting military personnel, yet its accurate assessment remains challenging because body mass index (BMI) does not distinguish between fat and lean mass; percent body fat (PBF) offers a more physiologically meaningful alternative. However, data on PBF-defined obesity prevalence and its predictors among elite Indian military personnel, such as Indian federal contingency force (IFCF) commandos, remain scarce.
